rationale: C20 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's discussion of the completed East German food-aid initiative. Both are presidential reply letters describing American food assistance to the people of Soviet-occupied eastern Germany, obstacles imposed by Communist or occupation authorities, and cooperation among United States, Federal German, and Berlin authorities. C06 is a closely related antecedent establishing the original food offer, while C13 shares the child's discussion of German employment and coordinated economic assistance but is less directly tied to the food program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the success which the cooperation of the Berlin authorities, the Federal Republic and the United States Government has achieved in bringing urgently needed food ... to the unfortunate people of Soviet occupied Germany
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is our joint purpose to aid the people of Eastern Germany ... I have directed the Secretary of State and the Director for Mutual Security to place quantities of these foodstuffs at your disposal
shared_material.explanation: The child reports the success of the same cooperative food-assistance machinery that C20 directs into operation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the many obstacles which the communist authorities have put in the way of these people
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in spite of the obstacles which the occupation authorities of that area have created
shared_material.explanation: The unusually close obstacles-and-authorities formulation links the child's retrospective account to C20's description of the program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: their welfare deeply concerns the free world which ... is determined to help them in every way possible
shared_material.parent_excerpt: relieving the suffering of the people of Eastern Germany in the best available manner
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the initiative as a continuing humanitarian commitment to East Germans despite Soviet obstruction.
